newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Buyers and sellers in K Mart.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Buyers and sellers in K Mart.

text.p: Buyers and sellers of options on shares of K Mart Corp were fairly busy Friday as the stock continued to feel pressure from some recent earnings downgrades, traders said.
In late action, K-Mart was down 3/8 at 12-3/8 on nearly 4.2 million shares in consolidated trading.
"We've got some people downgrading it, lowering earnings estimates and the stock's been very weak," said John Burnside, a market maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
Regarding the options activity, he said: "You've got some buyers and some sellers."
K Mart options activity was led by the Jun 12-1/2 put, which traded 6,935 contracts. The contract expires Saturday.
"There's a big roll going on in the June/July 12-1/2 put spread," Burnside said. "They're closing the June 12-1/2 puts and opening in the July 12-1/2 puts."
He added that a large U.S. institution was selling the September 12-1/2 calls and buying the September 15 calls.
The September 12-1/2 call traded about 3,890 contracts and the September 15 call traded 3,180.
"It sounds like that's a bearish strategy," Moby Waller, an analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, said of selling the September 12-1/2 calls and buying the 15s.

He said high open interest at the 15 strike, particularly in the September contract, where 18,740 contracts were open through Thursday, suggests the stock could hit resistance if it can recover from recent weakness.
The 12-1/2 level is key for the stock because that is about where the 100-day moving average is, he added.
"It's held above that (100-day moving average) on a weekly closing basis since last November," he said.
In general, Waller said K Mart shares look attractive because they are out of favor and there is heavy short interest.

Short interest in June on the stock was around 10 percent of the float, or 48 million and, according to Zachs, just seven out of 20 Wall Street analysts who follow the retailer rate it a buy, he said.
"We've tended to like both K Mart and Wal-Mart this year as out of favor retailers that are coming back in style," he said.
